reason: E1 directly supports the formation of a ~2 µm Ti-N layer under the specified conditions and its dramatic wear reduction, though the hypothesis overstates the layer thickness (3–4 µm vs. 2 µm). E3 supports the roles of compressive residual stress and mechanical support from the diffusion zone. E2 is cited as conflicting but actually highlights conditions under which fatigue may be reduced, which the hypothesis acknowledges as a boundary/uncertainty, so it does not undermine the core premises.
premises: Plasma nitriding in NH3-N2 (1:2) at 750 °C for 4 h forms a Ti-N compound layer ~2 µm thick on Ti-6Al-4V
The Ti-N compound layer is much harder than the substrate and eliminates stick-tear/plowing wear, yielding undetectable wear loss against bearing steel under 8 N load
The nitride layer and nitrogen diffusion zone generate compressive residual stresses that inhibit crack nucleation
The diffusion zone provides mechanical support to the brittle nitride layer
